title: Daily and weekly habits to extend your haircut's life
description: Practical local tips from 3D Cutz in Norwich to keep your haircut looking fresh between barber visits.

content.heading: Know what your cut needs
paragraphs: Different styles demand different upkeep. A skin fade or very short sides will show regrowth quickly, while longer, layered cuts tolerate a few extra weeks. When you’re in the chair at 3D Cutz, mention roughly how often you want to visit so the barber can tailor the cut for your schedule.
If you aren’t sure, ask for a maintenance plan — little changes to the length or taper at the edges can make a big difference to how long the whole haircut looks fresh.

content.heading: Daily care: washing, drying and styling
paragraphs: Adjust your washing routine to your hair type and activity. Most people don’t need to shampoo every day; over-washing strips natural oils and can flatten a cut. Use a conditioner on the mid-lengths and ends if your hair feels dry, and choose a gentle shampoo when you do wash.

Towel-dry gently and, if you use a hairdryer, do so on a low to medium heat to set the shape. Use a small amount of product — a light cream, matte clay or water-based pomade depending on the finish you want — and apply from the back forward to avoid flattening the roots.

content.heading: At-home upkeep and tools
paragraphs: A neat neckline and tidy edges keep a haircut looking sharp. A small trimmer can help manage the neckline between visits, but practise on a tiny area first and follow the natural hairline. If you prefer scissors, ask your barber to show a safe way to trim a fringe or remove a stray length.

If you’re unsure about DIY touch-ups, book a short maintenance appointment rather than attempting a big fix at home; a quick tidy from a professional preserves the shape and saves time in the long run.

content.heading: Little habits that make a big difference
paragraphs: Swap pillowcases regularly and avoid sleeping with hair wet — damp hair creases and loses shape overnight. Use dry shampoo on days you skip washing to absorb excess oil and add texture, which can revive a style instantly.

Protect your cut from the elements where possible: a quick towel-dry after rain and a comb-through with a little product will restore shape. Regularly checking in with your barber about product choices or minor adjustments will keep your cut working for your everyday life.
